sections.label: Fee Benchmarks procedure coverage
sections.summary: Fee Benchmarks cover about 220 of over 2,300 Table of Surgical Procedures procedures, and MOH should provide benchmarks for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The benchmarks align with the Table of Surgical Procedures or TOSP, a comprehensive list of over 2,300 procedures categorised by their complexity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, it is notable that only about 220 procedures or 9% of these procedures are listed in the Fee Benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The remaining 2,000-plus procedures do not yet have fee benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In comparison, GOF contained over 1,500 surgical fee recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To make the Fee Benchmarks a more effective and authoritative reference for patients, doctors and insurers, MOH should provide Fee Benchmarks for all the procedures in the Table of Surgical Procedures.

sections.label: Expanding panels and insurer payouts
sections.summary: Panels should admit all doctors who wish to join, and all insurers should use Fee Benchmarks to determine payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To provide patients with a wider choice of doctors, panels should be expanded to admit all doctors who wish to be on the panel, so that patients will not feel pressured to switch away from their preferred doctor just because that doctor is not on the panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to give greater assurance to patients that fees charged by their doctors will be covered by insurance, all insurers should use the Fee Benchmarks to determine their payouts.

sections.label: Itemised hospital bills by default
sections.summary: Doctors and hospitals should by default give detailed itemised charges, using a consistent MOH template listing base costs and mark-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Doctors and hospitals should be required to provide detailed itemisation of charges on their bills by default.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hospitals should list their base costs and mark-ups on drugs and consumables.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This itemisation should be made consistent across all hospitals, based on a transparent, prescriptive template set by MOH.

sections.label: Registering overcharging concerns
sections.summary: Patients and insurers should have a mechanism to register concerns about overcharging or over-servicing, with MOH setting up an independent arbitration unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead, patients and insurers should be provided with a mechanism to register their concerns about overcharging or over-servicing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I was glad to hear during Question Time earlier this morning that MOH is setting up an independent arbitration unit.

sections.label: Integrated Shield Plan coverage
sections.summary: Almost 70% of Singaporeans have an Integrated Shield Plan, with most premiums funded by MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Almost 70% of Singaporeans possess an Integrated Shield Plan and most premiums funded by their MediSave.

sections.label: MAS role on MHIC
sections.summary: MAS should take a more proactive role, having had two members on the 2016 task force but only observer status on the MHIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), as a regulator of insurers, should also take a more proactive role in this process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is notable that MAS had two committee members on the Health Insurance Task Force in 2016, but has only observer status on the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (MHIC) that was just set up last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Why not make them full committee members so that their inputs in the committee's deliberations will carry greater weight?

sections.label: Government healthcare spending tripled
sections.summary: Government healthcare spending tripled within a decade, from $3.7 billion in FY2010 to $11.3 billion in FY2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government spending on healthcare has tripled within a decade, from $3.7 billion in FY2010 to $11.3 billion in FY2019.

sections.label: Fee Benchmarks coverage of procedures
sections.summary: Fee Benchmarks cover 8% of the 2,300 TOSP procedures, chosen as they accounted for over 85% of cases and 75% of professional fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Although Fee Benchmarks have been published for only 8% of the 2,300 procedures listed in the Table of Surgical Procedures, or TOSP, these 200 procedures were selected as they accounted for more than 85% of the cases involving procedures and 75% of professional fees for procedures in the private sector.

sections.label: Doctors using Fee Benchmarks
sections.summary: Over 80% of 2019 fees were within benchmark upper limits, and MOH introduced 2020 benchmarks for anaesthetist and inpatient attendance fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Indeed, our early data showed that doctors have been taking reference from the benchmarks, with more than 80% of fees in 2019 within the upper limit of the benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In 2020, MOH further introduced new benchmarks for anaesthetist and inpatient attendance fees, and will continue to review and develop new areas of fee benchmarking with the Fee Benchmarks Advisory Committee.

sections.label: Bill granularity and price transparency
sections.summary: MOH will prescribe minimum bill granularity, and licensees must display common charges and provide financial counselling before service provision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH will prescribe the minimum level of granularity that must be reflected in patients' bills, which include categories such as consultation, medication and investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Just as importantly, licensees are required to display common charges prominently at their premises or on their websites and provide financial counselling for services which tend to generate significant bills prior to service provision, to ensure greater price transparency upfront and help patients make much more informed choices.

sections.label: Panel expansion and pre-authorisation
sections.summary: Pre-authorisation is the way to give all doctors access, panel sizes rose 40%, and IP premium changes need MOH approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: One is on the issue of expanding the panel to more doctors or in fact, to all doctors, and I have explained in the PQ reply that pre-authorisation is the way to go, to provide access to care by all doctors through the pre-authorisation route.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And in fact, panel sizes have increased by 40% in the last six months to a year, up to 70% of private specialists are already on at least one panel.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Any changes to IP premiums or terms and conditions, requires approval from MOH.

sections.label: Surgeons grading surgical procedures
sections.summary: Mr Gerald Giam may not be aware how surgeons grade surgical procedures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Gerald Giam may not be aware how the surgeons grade surgical procedures.

sections.label: Insurer data for common procedures
sections.summary: For common procedures, insurers have enough data sets to estimate a general ballpark and extrapolate for procedures without a benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, it is not something that is easily hardcoded because it can vary from case to case.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But, on the whole, for common procedures, there are enough data sets for insurers to get a certain sense of what the general ballpark is, and then use that to get an extrapolation of something that is not actually having a benchmark, but should fall somewhere in between.

sections.label: Panel, pre-authorisation, patient access
sections.summary: The panel only makes sense with fee arrangements, but enhancing pre-authorisation ensures all patients can access doctors for continuity of treatment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The panel only makes sense, if you have fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But, the key to ensure all patients have access to care is to enhance the pre-authorisation process, so all patients regardless of whether the doctors are on panel or not can have access to the doctor for continuity of treatment.
